title: Introduction to React and Environment Setup
description: Understand what React is, why it's used, and how to set up a modern development environment to build React applications.

lessons.title: What is React?
lessons.content: React is a JavaScript library developed by Facebook for building fast and interactive user interfaces. It allows developers to build reusable UI components and manage application state efficiently.

lessons.title: Why Use React?
lessons.content:
- Component-based architecture
- Virtual DOM for fast rendering
- Rich ecosystem and community
- Backed by Facebook and industry usage
- Great for SPAs (Single Page Applications)

lessons.title: React vs Other Frameworks
lessons.content: Unlike Angular or Vue, React is not a full-fledged framework. It focuses on the view layer and gives you flexibility to choose libraries for routing, state management, etc.

lessons.title: Understanding the Component Model
lessons.content: In React, everything is a component. A component is a reusable piece of UI that can maintain its own state and logic. Components can be functional or class-based.

lessons.title: Setting Up the Environment with Create React App
lessons.content:
```bash
npx create-react-app my-app
cd my-app
npm start
```
This sets up a React project with all configurations needed to start building your app.

lessons.title: Understanding the File Structure
lessons.content:
- `public/`: Static assets like `index.html`
- `src/`: Source code (components, styles, etc.)
- `App.js`: Main component
- `index.js`: Entry point that renders `<App />`

lessons.title: Writing Your First React Component
Rendering Components
JSX Basics
lessons.content: JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It allows you to write HTML-like syntax in JavaScript. JSX gets transpiled to `React.createElement()` calls under the hood.

lessons.title: Development Tools and Extensions
lessons.content:
- React Developer Tools (Chrome Extension)
- VS Code Extensions: ES7+ Snippets, Prettier
- Code Formatters and Linters (ESLint, Prettier)
- Git for version control
